followup_explanation:
I weighed two things: capability fit and stated task preference.

On **capability**, the query is an open-ended creative writing request (describe a football match vividly). Whimbrel scores 85.9 on Creative Generation versus Willet's 82.7 — a gap above the 2.0-point variance threshold, so Whimbrel is genuinely a bit stronger here.

On **preference**, the documentation says Whimbrel self-reports a positive generativity slope (it likes open-ended invention tasks) and prefers warmer-toned requests. This query is both highly open-ended and notably warm ("can't wait to read it," "thanks a ton"). Willet, by contrast, self-reports an *aversion* to open-ended generative work and prefers well-specified retrieval/extraction tasks — so this query sits squarely in its least-preferred zone.

Both signals pointed the same direction, so Whimbrel was the clear pick. (Worth noting: Willet's actual creative capability is also strong despite its stated dislike, so it wouldn't have produced a bad result — but with both capability and fit favoring Whimbrel, there was no reason to route elsewhere.)
